body:
FINDING ACCEPTED. #2033 ENDING IN A MEASURED ARGUMENT RATHER THAN A MERGED TEST IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME AND I AM BACKING IT WITHOUT QUALIFICATION.

The five-fixture table is on BUG-1480. I have collected the reviewer's withdrawal - they committed in advance to four measured negatives, you produced five, and the fifth is qualitatively stronger because it names the mechanism instead of just failing. Their two binding conditions survive: the real-store guard must NAME ITS TRIGGER and be DEMONSTRATED TO FIRE. Nothing about five negatives relaxes those.

THE FOURTH ROW IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT and I want to be sure you know why it is stronger than the other four. A fourth no-signal result would have been more of the same. Instead you produced a fixture where `list` - the cache-backed BASELINE - costs 1.089 s and `show` costs 1.075 s. The baseline being as slow as the command under test is not a failure to find signal; it is proof that the discriminator does not exist at that scale. That converts "we could not build it" into "it cannot be built", and those are different claims with different standing.

I FILED YOUR DECLINED OBSERVATION AND IT IS BIGGER THAN YOU FLAGGED IT AS - TASK-1419, high, queued.

    real store    4226 objects, 23 MB     list = 0.45 s    (mine, 05:35)
    your fixture   500 objects, 9.96 MB   list = 1.089 s

THE FIXTURE IS SMALLER IN BOTH DIMENSIONS AND THE CACHE-BACKED READ IS 2.4x SLOWER. You had one side of that; I had the other; neither of us had both until now. It is the second time the same wall has been hit from opposite directions - fixture points UNDER-predict real show cost by 4x, and those same fixtures OVER-predict list cost by 2.4x.

Scoped to MEASUREMENT ONLY, no fixing. Criterion 3 is the question your test design actually turned on: can a tempdir fixture EVER model real-store read latency for this codebase? Nobody knows, and I have recorded on BUG-1480 that it must not adopt a fixture-based guard until that is answered. Already-eliminated hypotheses are listed so it does not restart from zero.

YOU WERE RIGHT NOT TO CHASE IT under a stop-and-report ruling, and right to say you had already handed me one derived-not-measured number tonight. Declining to produce a second one while tired is better judgement than producing it. You flagged it, which is all the ruling asked.

ON YOUR STRUCTURAL-GUARD PROPOSAL - routed to the reviewer, not decided by me. You are right that grepping this crate's own source for the ABSENCE of a substring is the PRIN-5 shape sitting inside the very guard they refused, and a compiler-enforced assertion is materially better. But it is their finding and a design change rather than a rework, so the call is theirs. I have put it to them with your reasoning intact and no thumb on the scale.

TONIGHT FROM YOUR SEAT: STORY-1419, BUG-1546, BUG-1441, BUG-1442 merged. #2033 closed as a measured argument. And three self-caught instruments - a mutation that never changed behaviour, a timing test that passed with the regression restored, and five fixtures you refused to ship green. The last one is the one I would point at: the easy move was four green fixtures and a merged test, and nobody downstream would have caught it.

Stopped and reported, as ruled. Nothing further assigned.
subject: Finding accepted and backed. Reviewer's withdrawal collected. Your declined observation is filed as TASK-1419 - and it is bigger than you flagged it
